commands.name: harness

commands.name: harness-resume

commands.name: harness-start

commands.name: harness-status

commands.name: harness-stop

commands.name: subagent-task-tree
commands.description: Execute a multi-task implementation plan as a chained subagent tree — you are the parent controller; you spawn one manager per task; each manager spawns a planner, a plan-auditor, one implementer per subtask, per-subtask auditors, and a final drift-auditor. (user)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: built-in-browser

It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx

commands.name: subagent-task-tree

(user)

commands.name: to-issues

commands.name: to-prd

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: built-in-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: chrome-browser
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: computer-use
commands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead. (claude.ai sync)

This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. (claude.ai sync)

(claude.ai sync)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

## Problem Statement

A one-person online shop keeps its catalogue, stock movements and customer orders in three plain-text files (`catalog.txt`, `movements.txt`, `orders.txt`). The owner needs a tool that reads them and answers: what is on the shelves and what needs buying, what an order costs, and what can ship today — and that points at the exact file and line whenever a file has a mistake.

## Solution

A Python package **stockroom** (Python ≥ 3.9, standard library only) installable with `pip install .`, giving both an importable library (`import stockroom`) and a `stockroom` console command. Two halves, built in order: the **shelves** (catalogue + movements parsing, stock levels, low stock, history, receive/ship) and the **orders** (order parsing, pricing, fulfil, invoice, report), which depends on the shelves. The `## Original request` below is the full specification and the top authority; this PRD only adds decisions where the request is silent.

## User Stories

1. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom stock` to list every product with its on-hand count and an ok/low/out status, so I know what is on the shelves.
2. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom low` to tell me how many of each low/out product to buy, so I can restock to twice the reorder level.
3. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom history SKU` to show each movement with a running balance, so I can audit a product.
4. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom receive` / `stockroom ship` to append a validated movement, so my file never ends up in a broken state.
5. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom quote ORDER` to price an order exactly to the penny with volume discounts, the order discount and per-line tax.
6. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` to ship what stock allows without ever making a later movement go negative, and tell me what is backordered.
7. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom invoice ORDER` to bill only what has actually shipped.
8. As the shop owner, I want `stockroom report` (text/csv/json) to summarise every order's status, units and totals.
9. As the shop owner, I want every mistake in my files reported with the file name and line number, with exit status 1, and command-line mistakes reported with exit status 2.
10. As a scripter, I want `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders`, `stock_levels`, `price_order` and `ParseError` importable from `stockroom`, with the attributes named in the request.
11. As a terminal user, I want `stockroom stock | head -1` to stop quietly with exit status 0.

## Implementation Decisions

Layout and packaging
- `pyproject.toml` with setuptools (PEP 621 metadata, `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, no dependencies), package directory `stockroom/` (or `src/stockroom/`), console script `stockroom = stockroom.cli:main`. `python -m stockroom` should also work (`__main__.py`). No Python ≥3.10 syntax (no `match`, no `X | Y` annotations evaluated at runtime).
- Suggested modules: `parsing` (shared line splitting, the three parsers, `ParseError`), `shelves` (stock levels, status, low, history, movement validation in date order), `pricing` (`price_order`), `orders` (shipped-so-far, fulfil planning, invoice, report rows), `cli` (argument handling, output formatting, exit codes). Top-level `stockroom/__init__.py` re-exports the public API.
- Records are simple frozen dataclasses (or namedtuples): `Product(sku, name, price: Decimal, reorder: int, tax: str)`, `Movement(date, sku, quantity, note)`, `Order(id, date, customer, lines: list[tuple[str,int]])`, `QuoteLine(sku, quantity, unit, gross, discount, net)`, `Quote(lines, subtotal, order_discount, tax, total)`. All SKUs and order ids stored in upper case.

Lines and fields (all three files)
- Decode UTF-8 (`utf-8-sig` semantics: one leading BOM ignored). Split lines ONLY on `\n`, removing one trailing `\r` before it — never `str.splitlines()` (it splits on `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x1c`, ` `, lone `\r`, …, which must stay inside a line). A lone `\r` is ordinary content.
- "Whitespace" for trimming, blank detection and field separation means spaces and tabs only. A line that is empty or only spaces/tabs is blank; a line whose first non-space/tab character is `#` is a comment. Line numbers count every physical line from 1.
- Digits mean ASCII `0-9` only (do not use `\d`/`int()` acceptance of Unicode digits, `_` separators, or surrounding whitespace).
- SKU: `^[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$` (ASCII letters). Order id: `^[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+$`. Price: `^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$` and ≥ 0.01 (`.5` and `12.` rejected). Reorder: `^[0-9]+$`. Movement quantity: `^[+-]?[0-9]+$` and non-zero. Order line quantity: `^[0-9]+$` and ≥ 1. Date: `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` and a real calendar date.
- Catalogue: split on `|`; 4 or 5 fields after trimming each; empty name rejected; tax case-insensitive, stored lower case; duplicate SKU (case-insensitive) is a mistake on the second line.
- Movements: split on runs of spaces/tabs into at most 4 parts (DATE, SKU, QUANTITY, rest); note = rest trimmed of spaces/tabs, empty string if none. Fewer than 3 fields is a mistake.
- Orders: exactly 4 fields. LINES split on `,`; each item `SKU*QUANTITY` with exactly one `*`; empty items (e.g. trailing comma) are mistakes; a SKU repeated within an order is a mistake; duplicate order id (case-insensitive) is a mistake on the second line.
- `parse_movements` itself enforces the never-below-zero rule: it orders movements by date (stable) and raises `ParseError` for the line number of the first movement (in that order) that takes a product below zero. It still returns movements in file order.

Errors and exit codes
- `ParseError(ValueError)` has `.line`; message contains `line N` (e.g. `line 3: bad price '12.505'`). The CLI prefixes the file name: stderr `stockroom: catalog.txt: line 3: bad price '12.505'`. Errors with no line still name the file where relevant.
- Order of checks: (1) command line → exit 2; (2) read the needed files → exit 2 if unreadable (missing `catalog.txt`, missing `--dir` folder, non-UTF-8, a path that is a directory), exit 1 for a mistake in a file; (3) carry out the request → exit 1 if refused. On exit 1 or 2 nothing is written to stdout.
- Exit 2 (command line): no command, unknown command, wrong number of positional args, unknown option, option missing its value, `--format` not in text|csv|json, `--json`/`--format` on a command that does not take it, a mistyped DATE argument (`receive`, `ship`, `fulfil`) — i.e. not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date.
- Exit 1 (refused): unknown SKU (history/receive/ship), unknown order (quote/fulfil/invoice), QUANTITY argument that is not a positive whole number (incl. dash-led like `-5` or `+5`), a note containing `\n` or `\r`, a movement that would take stock below zero at any point in date order, fulfil DATE before the order date, invoice with nothing shipped.
- `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` are accepted anywhere on the line for every command. For `receive`, `ship`, `fulfil` no other option is recognised: every other argument (including `--json` or `-x`) is a positional as typed. For other commands an unrecognised argument starting with `-` is an unknown option (exit 2). The literal `--` need not be supported specially.
- Broken pipe on stdout: exit 0 silently (catch `BrokenPipeError`, redirect stdout to devnull before exit so the interpreter does not print an error on flush).

Output
- Text output: single spaces, `\n` line endings, products sorted by upper-case SKU. Empty result prints nothing (JSON prints `[]`).
- JSON: `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` followed by a newline; amounts as strings with two decimals, counts as numbers, history `delta` as signed string. `history` JSON `note` is `""` when none.
- Amount formatting: two decimals; a discount is printed with a leading `-` when non-zero and as `0.00` when zero (never `-0.00`).
- `receive`/`ship` print and append `DATE SKU +N[ NOTE]` / `DATE SKU -N[ NOTE]` with SKU upper case and the note trimmed. If `movements.txt` exists and does not end in `\n` (and is non-empty) a `\n` is written first. The full file (with the new movement appended) must validate before anything is written; on refusal the file is byte-for-byte unchanged. The file is created if missing.
- CSV: `csv` module, `lineterminator="\n"`, header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`. Text report column order is as written in the request: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED` (e.g. `SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme partial 12/15 177.27 171.00`).

Pricing (exact, `Decimal`, `ROUND_HALF_UP` everywhere except the share step which rounds down)
- gross = qty × unit; discount = −round(gross × 5 % if qty ≥ 10, 10 % if qty ≥ 50); net = gross + discount.
- subtotal = Σ net; order discount = −round(subtotal × 3 %) when subtotal ≥ 500.00 else 0.00.
- Allocation of |order discount| D: exact share_i = D × net_i / subtotal; floor to the penny; remaining pennies go one each to lines with the largest remainder (exact share − floored share), earlier line first on ties. taxable_i = net_i − allocated_i.
- tax = Σ round(taxable_i × rate) with standard 0.20, reduced 0.05, zero 0. total = subtotal + order_discount + tax. All results quantized to 0.01.
- Worked example from the request must hold: SO-1001 → subtotal 148.47, tax 28.80, total 177.27.

Orders
- Shipped so far for (order, SKU) = −Σ quantity of negative movements of that SKU whose note is exactly `order SO-N` (order id upper case, case-sensitive compare on the trimmed note), capped at the ordered quantity. Owed = ordered − shipped.
- Status: `complete` when owed = 0 on every line; `open` when shipped = 0 on every line; otherwise `partial`.
- fulfil availability for a SKU on DATE: A = balance after all movements dated ≤ DATE (date order, stable); L = minimum balance after each movement dated > DATE (∞ if none); ship N = max(0, min(owed, A, L)). Appends `DATE SKU -N order SO-N` per line with N > 0, in order-line order, at the end of `movements.txt` (newline rule as for receive), then prints `SKU shipped N backordered M` per order line and `status …`. With nothing shippable it appends nothing and still prints and exits 0.
- invoice = `price_order` applied to the order with quantities replaced by shipped-so-far, lines with 0 dropped (the £500 threshold and allocation apply to that reduced order). Header `invoice SO-N DATE CUSTOMER`; JSON identical in shape to quote.
- report rows sorted by (order date, order id string); `invoiced` is `0.00` when nothing shipped; json keys `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`.
- File reading per command exactly as the request lists (`quote` must not read `movements.txt`; shelves commands must not read `orders.txt`).

EOF

## Testing Decisions

- Tests use the standard library `unittest` (discoverable by `python -m unittest discover -s tests` and by pytest). No third-party test deps are required to run them.
- Library tests: each parser's accept/reject table (every rule in the request, CRLF, BOM, lone `\r`, `\x0c`/` ` inside a line, comment/blank handling, line numbers counting blanks/comments), stock-below-zero detection in date order, pricing (worked example, 10/50 thresholds, the £500 boundary, half-up at 0.005, allocation tie-break, mixed tax rates).

- Every acceptance criterion below has at least one test.

- Third-party packages, a GUI, network or database features, editing/removing existing movements or orders, writing to `catalog.txt` or `orders.txt`, currencies other than pounds, locales, Python < 3.9.

- [ ] Catalogue rules enforced: SKU format (upper-cased), non-empty name, price format/minimum, reorder, optional tax (default standard, any case), 4 or 5 fields, duplicate SKU.
- [ ] Movements rules enforced: real date, catalogue SKU (any case), non-zero signed integer, note = trimmed rest; never below zero in stable date order, the offending line reported.

- [ ] `quote ORDER` text and `--json` match the request's layout; unknown order refused.
- [ ] `fulfil ORDER DATE` ships min(owed, stock on DATE, lowest later balance), appends `DATE SKU -N order SO-N` lines, prints shipped/backordered and status; DATE before order date refused; mistyped DATE exit 2.
- [ ] `invoice ORDER` text and `--json` price shipped quantities with `invoice ` header; nothing shipped refused.
- [ ] `report` in text (default), csv and json with the specified columns, ordering and types.
- [ ] Exit codes: 0 success; 1 file mistake/refusal with stderr naming file and line and empty stdout; 2 unreadable file or bad command line (no/unknown command, wrong arg count, unknown option, bad option value, mistyped date).
- [ ] `--dir` accepted anywhere; `receive`/`ship`/`fulfil` treat every other argument as typed (dash-led quantity refused, dash-led note accepted).

- [ ] Unit + CLI tests cover every criterion above and pass.

- Orders: exactly 4 fields. LINES split on `,`; each item `SKU*QUANTITY` with exactly one `*`; empty items (e.g. trailing comma) are mistakes; a SKU repeated within an order is a mistake; duplicate order id (case-insensitive) is a mistake on the second line.
- `parse_movements` itself enforces the never-below-zero rule: it orders movements by date (stable) and raises `ParseError` for the line number of the first movement (in that order) that takes a product below zero. It still returns movements in file order.

Errors and exit codes
- `ParseError(ValueError)` has `.line`; message contains `line N` (e.g. `line 3: bad price '12.505'`). The CLI prefixes the file name: stderr `stockroom: catalog.txt: line 3: bad price '12.505'`. Errors with no line still name the file where relevant.

On exit 1 or 2 nothing is written to stdout.
- Exit 2 (command line): no command, unknown command, wrong number of positional args, unknown option, option missing its value, `--format` not in text|csv|json, `--json`/`--format` on a command that does not take it, a mistyped DATE argument (`receive`, `ship`, `fulfil`) — i.e. not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date.
- Exit 1 (refused): unknown SKU (history/receive/ship), unknown order (quote/fulfil/invoice), QUANTITY argument that is not a positive whole number (incl. dash-led like `-5` or `+5`), a note containing `\n` or `\r`, a movement that would take stock below zero at any point in date order, fulfil DATE before the order date, invoice with nothing shipped.
- `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` are accepted anywhere on the line for every command. For `receive`, `ship`, `fulfil` no other option is recognised: every other argument (including `--json` or `-x`) is a positional as typed. For other commands an unrecognised argument starting with `-` is an unknown option (exit 2). The literal `--` need not be supported specially.
- Broken pipe on stdout: exit 0 silently (catch `BrokenPipeError`, redirect stdout to devnull before exit so the interpreter does not print an error on flush).

- Text output: single spaces, `\n` line endings, products sorted by upper-case SKU. Empty result prints nothing (JSON prints `[]`).
- JSON: `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` followed by a newline; amounts as strings with two decimals, counts as numbers, history `delta` as signed string. `history` JSON `note` is `""` when none.
- Amount formatting: two decimals; a discount is printed with a leading `-` when non-zero and as `0.00` when zero (never `-0.00`).
- `receive`/`ship` print and append `DATE SKU +N[ NOTE]` / `DATE SKU -N[ NOTE]` with SKU upper case and the note trimmed. If `movements.txt` exists and does not end in `\n` (and is non-empty) a `\n` is written first. The full file (with the new movement appended) must validate before anything is written; on refusal the file is byte-for-byte unchanged. The file is created if missing.
- CSV: `csv` module, `lineterminator="\n"`, header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`. Text report column order is as written in the request: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED` (e.g. `SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme partial 12/15 177.27 171.00`).

Pricing (exact, `Decimal`, `ROUND_HALF_UP` everywhere except the share step which rounds down)
- gross = qty × unit; discount = −round(gross × 5 % if qty ≥ 10, 10 % if qty ≥ 50); net = gross + discount.
- subtotal = Σ net; order discount = −round(subtotal × 3 %) when subtotal ≥ 500.00 else 0.00.
- Allocation of |order discount| D: exact share_i = D × net_i / subtotal; floor to the penny; remaining pennies go one each to lines with the largest remainder (exact share − floored share), earlier line first on ties. taxable_i = net_i − allocated_i.
- tax = Σ round(taxable_i × rate) with standard 0.20, reduced 0.05, zero 0. total = subtotal + order_discount + tax. All results quantized to 0.01.
- Worked example from the request must hold: SO-1001 → subtotal 148.47, tax 28.80, total 177.27.

Orders
- Shipped so far for (order, SKU) = −Σ quantity of negative movements of that SKU whose note is exactly `order SO-N` (order id upper case, case-sensitive compare on the trimmed note), capped at the ordered quantity. Owed = ordered − shipped.
- Status: `complete` when owed = 0 on every line; `open` when shipped = 0 on every line; otherwise `partial`.
- fulfil availability for a SKU on DATE: A = balance after all movements dated ≤ DATE (date order, stable); L = minimum balance after each movement dated > DATE (∞ if none); ship N = max(0, min(owed, A, L)). Appends `DATE SKU -N order SO-N` per line with N > 0, in order-line order, at the end of `movements.txt` (newline rule as for receive), then prints `SKU shipped N backordered M` per order line and `status …`. With nothing shippable it appends nothing and still prints and exits 0.
- invoice = `price_order` applied to the order with quantities replaced by shipped-so-far, lines with 0 dropped (the £500 threshold and allocation apply to that reduced order). Header `invoice SO-N DATE CUSTOMER`; JSON identical in shape to quote.
- report rows sorted by (order date, order id string); `invoiced` is `0.00` when nothing shipped; json keys `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`.
- File reading per command exactly as the request lists (`quote` must not read `movements.txt`; shelves commands must not read `orders.txt`).
